Can-Do (A2): I can describe a journey, destination, accommodation and way of travelling using appropriate travel vocabulary.
I can describe my own or another traveller's qualities, faults and habits, placing and agreeing common adjectives correctly.
I can discuss different travel options and reach a decision about where, when and how to go.
I can justify a choice with parce que, grâce à or à cause de, distinguishing a neutral, positive or negative cause.
I can use en for a complement introduced by de and y for a place or complement introduced by à, placing the pronoun before its verb.
I can describe a physical or personal challenge and explain what I find easy or difficult.
I can express the opposites of toujours, tout and tout le monde with ne… jamais, ne… rien and ne… personne.
I can encourage and reassure someone who is hesitating or finding a challenge difficult.
I can invite someone, respond to hesitation, and insist politely without ending the exchange.
I can work with others to design and present a coherent virtual journey, explaining and defending our choices.
I can describe what I see, hear, smell, taste and touch in a place or experience.
I can identify and compare the most, least, best and worst examples within a group.
I can describe and give a simple appreciation of an artwork, performance or cultural experience.

Topic: Interrogative pronouns lequel, laquelle, lesquels, lesquelles
Can-Do (A2): I can ask and answer which one or ones someone prefers when the choices are already known.
I can identify an emotion from a situation and say how an experience makes me feel.
I can form and use common manner adverbs to describe how an action is performed or experienced.

Topic: Buying an artwork or decorative object
Can-Do (A2): I can handle a purchase by explaining what I want, asking about price and payment, choosing an item and completing the transaction.
I can write a friendly, organised email that gives several practical suggestions and links them clearly.
I can record and introduce a short soundscape and explain the sensations or emotions it creates.

Topic: Three days of well-being — collaborative mission
Can-Do (A2): I can compare ideas, ask for advice and negotiate a three-day cultural and well-being programme with a group.
I can describe a change in style or appearance and explain what changed and why.

Topic: Passé composé and imparfait in a past narrative
Can-Do (A2): I can distinguish background description and ongoing circumstances from completed events when recounting a change or story.
I can describe family relationships and use a family tree or other clues to explain how people are related.
I can explain why something happened and state its result using a range of simple cause-and-consequence links.
I can identify and describe an object precisely and explain where it came from and why it matters to someone.

Topic: Indefinite quantities — quelques, chaque, tous, plusieurs
Can-Do (A2): I can refer to an exact or non-exact number of people, objects or occasions with the appropriate indefinite quantity word.
I can reopen contact, ask after someone and their family, respond with news, and close the exchange naturally.
I can recount a short personal or family story in chronological order, using time markers and appropriate past tenses.

Topic: Family recipe for happiness — cultural project
Can-Do (A2): I can gather and present a family saying, custom or 'recipe for happiness' and explain its significance.

Topic: Our family has secrets — collaborative mission
Can-Do (A2): I can combine clues with a group to invent and present a coherent family history or secret.
I can offer, request and respond to a practical service and say what I am willing to do for others.
I can give instructions or encouragement with an imperative and replace the recipient with lui or leur when appropriate.
I can describe a problem in a home and propose changes to its rooms, furniture, equipment or decoration.

Topic: Expressing purpose with pour and afin de
Can-Do (A2): I can explain the purpose of an action or home improvement using pour or afin de followed by an infinitive.

Topic: Conditions and wishes with si and the conditional
Can-Do (A2): I can imagine a different situation, state a condition, and explain what I would do or like as a result.
I can describe and compare accommodation by type, location, size, rooms, facilities and household objects.
I can identify a common administrative service and explain the main steps or documents needed for a simple procedure.
I can make a complaint, explain what went wrong and press for an appropriate response while showing dissatisfaction clearly.
I can write a concise accommodation review that evaluates key features and clearly recommends or advises against the place.

Topic: Renovating a community building — collaborative mission
Can-Do (A2): I can propose, sketch and defend a plan for renovating a building to meet a community's needs and wishes.
